title: Fast UGC ad-tool promo bed
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 960,000 samples (20.0 s at 30 fps = 600 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 20-second punchy SaaS-promo bed in B minor at 120 BPM (1 beat = 15 frames, 10 bars). Frame 0: hit (kick + 808-ish sine sub on B1 + short noise crash). Frames 0-60: filtered intro, drums at 800 Hz low-pass opening up, typing-style clicks on 16ths (URL paste moment), a 'paste' pop on frame 45. Frame 60: full beat: tight kick on 1 and 3, clap on 2 and 4, 16th hats, sidechained (−6 dB pump, 150 ms release) supersaw chords Bm9 → Gmaj7 → D → A6, gliding 808 bass. Frames 120-360: a metric-flash tick (bright 6 kHz sine blip + 1 ms click, 60 ms) on every beat 2 and the '&' of 4, and a quick stutter (4 x 1/32 repeats of the chord) on frames 180, 240 and 300 for clip-cycling cuts. Frame 450: launch-toggle accent (two-tone up-chirp E6→B6 with a soft switch click). Frames 525-540: 1-beat drop-out. Frame 540: end-card hit on Bm(add9), tail fades to 0 by frame 600. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: Punchy B-minor SaaS promo bed at 120 BPM: supersaw stabs, 808, metric ticks, chord stutters, launch chirp, drop-out then end-card hit.
